My wife and I are both attracted towards a more minimalist life... we both have lived it before and miss it. Most of my stuff at this point consists of tools, things for creating and fixing. Whether mechanical or electronical, I take pride in building things or keeping things running. How do you balance your desire for minimalism with your interest in self sufficiency to one degree or another? It is somewhat difficult, for instance, to "live minimally", but also keep the tools and facilities for repairing your one automobile. Gardening, food processing, and light farming requires a not insignificant number of "things". I feel we are moving towards a "large garage, small house" type situation, but am not sure if that will just feel like more work... has anyone else faced a similar debacle on one scale or another?
How do you balance minimalism and some degree of self sufficiency?

I figure the point of minimalism is to cut down the number of possessions to the bare minimum of those that are meaningful and essential for you.

In this case I wouldn't say your tools are excessive. They are valuable to your psyche and thus your well-being. So there's no harm in having them. In fact I'd argue that not having them would be detrimental to you.

On a practical level, it sounds like these tools are doing a lot of good for your family and your household.

No one is keeping score of how many possessions you have so if you love them, keep them.
